title: Japan and Denmark as his favorite places to travel
summary: He loved Japan above all, for its countryside and the way people treated him like a king, and also spoke highly of Denmark.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did George, you say, what were the places he went, like Japan the best. Did he, can you say anything about that or traveling or where he likes to be out of the way and so on?

Well, Japan was his favorite. Why? I believe it was the countryside, the people themselves. He liked, he liked all traveling. He was one that, I believe, much of his illness that he had had was the fact that he couldn't travel. Toward the end, especially when his feet started getting in trouble. He liked Denmark quite a bit. He always spoke to Denmark quite highly. And Papa Boo. But everything was Japan. I don't know. He always said, he says, Carol, when I get better, he said, we're going to go back to Japan. He said, we may just stay there permanently. I mean, he just enjoyed it. He loved it. The people were nice to him. He said they treated him, a human. He put it in that type of term. And every time he left, he left part of them, he said, in Japan. He's got pictures and pictures and pictures and pictures of Japan that were taken. And I guess it's the fact that everybody idolized himself. I mean, everybody just spelled out when he came. He was treated like a king. And he loved it. He said he loved every bit of it. He said he didn't know how he would adjust to it. He adjusted quicker, more quicker than he thought he would.
